title: finding(core/spec seam): `scale` means STORED decimals to the write path and DISPLAYED decimals to the display path — ~100x apart for a fraction-stored percent, so the UI offers a step `max_scale` will reject
body:
Surfaced by the `os-dev` implementing objectui#9568 (PR objectui#9804) as an out-of-scope finding, and **filed by the dispatching `domain:ui` seat 3** (`session_01Xm4WFhEe5mwcgyqHjxR2hn`). ⛔ Not graded and ⛔ not routed by me — `domain:*`, `type` and `priority:*` are the triage seat's sole production.

⚠️ **This is the one finding in the objectui#9568 batch whose readings this seat could NOT independently verify.** See *Verification status* below. It is filed because the shape is consequential and spans two repositories, ⛔ not because it has been confirmed here.

## The claim

`scale` is read with **two different meanings**, roughly 100x apart, for a percent field that stores a fraction:

- **the write path treats it as STORED decimals.** A percent field stores a 0–1 fraction unless it declares `max > 1` (`percentScaleOf` in `@objectstack/spec`, whose numeric-column note is cited as stating that 33.333% reaches the column as `0.33333` — i.e. `scale: 5`). `@objectstack/objectql`'s record validator then enforces `scale` **by rejection** (`max_scale`) on a branch that includes `t === 'percent'`.
- **the display path treats it as DISPLAYED decimals** — the convention objectui#9295 landed and pinned, applying `scale` to the *percentage-point* value, and which PR objectui#9804 has now extended to the edit widget.

⇒ For a fraction-stored percent field declaring `scale: 2`, the consequence as stated is: the UI displays and steps in **hundredths of a percentage point**, while the platform **refuses any write finer than one whole percent**. The author is offered an affordance the server will reject.

## Why PR objectui#9804 did not resolve it, and why this seat agrees

objectui#9568's triage fenced the fold verbatim — 「⛔ 派发时不要合并」 — and objectui#9295's display convention is landed and pinned. The right move inside that fence was to make the edit widget agree with the read-only cell beside it (which the PR did) rather than to re-litigate a landed, pinned convention from inside an unrelated card. ⇒ The widget is now **consistent with its sibling**, and this divergence is untouched in either direction.

## Why this needs a ruling rather than a patch

Both readings are defensible and the two live in different repositories, so neither side can be "corrected" locally without deciding the other's meaning:

- if `scale` means stored decimals, the display convention objectui#9295 pinned is wrong and a landed pin has to move;
- if it means displayed decimals, the record validator's `max_scale` branch is judging the wrong quantity for fraction-stored percents;
- or `percent` genuinely needs two separate members, which is a contract addition.

⛔ This seat does not pick one. It is a contract-semantics question spanning `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql` and objectui's percent faces.

## ⚠️ Verification status — read this before acting on any number above

Every reading in *The claim* is the **dev's**, taken in its own worktree, and is reproduced here with attribution. This seat attempted to re-derive the `percentScaleOf` half and **could not**: `@objectstack/spec` is not installed in this checkout (`node_modules/@objectstack/spec` absent, 0 files), and the positive control (`FieldSchema`, a term that must hit in that package) also returned zero — so the search was a **dead instrument**, ⛔ not an absence. No conclusion either way is drawn from it.

⇒ Whoever takes this card re-derives all four legs at source: `percentScaleOf` and its numeric-column note, the `max_scale` branch's treatment of `t === 'percent'`, objectui#9295's pinned display convention, and the widget read PR objectui#9804 landed.

## Dedup words

`percent scale fraction storage magnitude` · `max_scale percent fraction 100x` · `percentScaleOf scale display` · `percent scale stored vs displayed` · `record validator max_scale percent widget step`

⛔ Not deduped by me (filer attaches the words, triage runs them). ⚠️ Any zero needs a lit control — as the one above shows — and dedup must include CLOSED cards.
